Guidance & outlook: Going forward, we expect agriculture growth to return to the 15-16% range.
We have guided for around 45% and we expect it to remain in that range.
Going forward, I expect to raise between USD1.5 billion and USD2 billion.
Growth & demand: Deposits grew by 13.40%, while advances grew by 13.89%, leav ing a gap of only around 40 b asis po ints.
Corporate advances grew by 11.49%, while RAM advances grew by 14.80%.
Growth was negative during the initial two months, but it picked up thereafter, resulting in growth of around 10%.
Margins & costs: The negative impact from MCLR repricing, estimated at around 2 basis points, should be offset by a 2 -3 basis-point benefit from bulk- deposit repricing.
Margins may expand marginally by around 2-3 basis points.
The cost will not be materially lower; compared with a deposit cost of around 6.0-6.5%, the overall funding cost may not decline significantly.
Capex & expansion: So far, stress is not visible, but if something emerges, we have the capacity to absorb it.
There is currently no major trigger for further margin expansion unless interest rates rise or further repricing occurs.
Therefore, we do not expect meaningful margin compression or expansion from here, but the upper end of the guidance range is achievable.
Balance sheet & cash: Borrowings are available at around 5.00-5.25%, whereas even short-duration bulk deposits of 30 or 60 days can cost at least 100-150 basis points more.
As the Managing Director explained, we use borrowings as far as possible within our per mitted borrowing limits, with the balance funded through deposits.
The use of borrowings enabled us to maintain an LCR of 123%.
Risks & challenges: Return on assets declined by 3 basis points year- on-year but improved by 3 basis points sequentially.
We could have maintained the earlier level, but the net NPA ratio would then have declined further from 0.15% to 0.14% or 0.13%, therefore, we are co mfortable with the current position.
Credit cost declined from 0.47% in March 2026 to 0.23%.

Guidance & outlook: Global headline inflation is expected to increase to 4.4 percent in 2026 before easing to 3.7 percent in 2027, reflecting supply side pressures emanating from energy and transport disruptions.
Under the PM Mudra Yojana (including RRBs), the Bank achieved 100 percent of its annual target, disbursing ₹15,718 Crore against a target of ₹15,700 Crore.
Under the Atal Pension Yojana, the Bank added 6.05 lakh new enrolments during FY26, achieving an Average Accounts Per Branch of 104 against the proportionate target of 100.
Growth & demand: The IMF lowered its forecast by 0.2 percentage points, projecting global growth at 3.1 percent in 2026 and 3.2 percent in 2027, below the average of 3.7 percent for the period from year 2000 to 2019.

According to official data under the revised GDP series (base year 2022-23), real GDP growth rose to 7.8 percent year on year in Q3 FY26, driven by firm private consumption, steady capital formation, buoyant service activities, and sustained momentum in manufacturing.
Retail advances grew by 19 percent, agriculture credit by 11 percent, and MSME advances by 16 percent, reflecting a balanced and inclusive growth strategy aligned with national priorities.
Margins & costs: RBI projected CPI inflation for FY27 at 4.6 percent, with core inflation remaining under control.
Operating profit rose by 5 percent to ₹19,916 Crore, while net interest income grew by 7 percent to ₹26,915 Crore, reflecting stable core income performance and effective cost management.
Despite a competitive interest rate environment and industry-wide margin pressures, the Bank sustained a healthy Net Interest Margin (NIM) of 3.24 percent, demonstrating our balance sheet resilience.
Capex & expansion: High frequency indicators such as expansionary PMIs, strong GST collections, and sustained credit growth in FY26 reflect steady momentum.
The Bank recorded healthy expansion across key parameters.
The Bank continued to invest in employee development and institutional capacity building.
Balance sheet & cash: Overall, the global growth outlook remains weak but broadly stable, notwithstanding significant downside risks from prolonged geopolitical tensions, tighter financial conditions, and higher public debt.

Credit growth was driven through thematic retail campaigns, focused initiatives in housing and mortgage lending, and tailored solutions in agriculture and MSME segments, including dairy, tractor , cluster based financing, and secured working capital products.
Risks & challenges: Macroeconomic Overview Navigating Renewed Headwinds In FY26, the global economy entered a more uncertain phase amid renewed geopolitical shocks and rising macroeconomic risks from the Middle East conflicts.
Resilience Amid Policy Easing and Volatility During FY26 amid heightened global uncertainty and volatile capital flows, the domestic banking sector operated well.
Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA%) to Gross Advance declined to 1.98 percent, while Net Non-Performing Asset (NNPA%) reduced further to a record low of 0.15 percent.
